study.question: Can packing only the varying conditional hash tables eliminate the observed packed-field memory penalty and reduce measured cost while retaining the shared reference numerical function? Does omission interact with packing despite its earlier null/adverse speed result?
study.hypothesis: Observation: round22 shared partition preserved AUC0.6203373141662112 and same-checkpoint strict equality in all cells; shared_packed had490.7464s wall and471328256 peak bytes versus shared serial493.2166s and396027904bytes. Its packing speed difference was only0.50% wall/0.57%train/0.36%inference, too small to call robust. Round21 native sparse omission preserved AUC but was slower(516.2056s versus511.4722s wall); analytic constants changed AUC to0.6200344118940478 despite a9.81e-8 diagnostic identity difference. Proposed execution mechanism: halve packed mass storage by constructing only the two varying groups per field, while preserving conditional field distributions, complete-pair supports and native matched-constant operations. This may reduce packed temporary memory and dense reduction work enough to compensate sparse reconstruction overhead. No kernel-launch or bandwidth bottleneck is established without profiling. This is an unverified execution-cost hypothesis, not a new predictive information mechanism.

nearest_work.difference: Inherit the exact shared partition, static and recency/action/histogram features, hash estimator and readouts. Activate inherited native sparse serial computation and add packed two-varying-group execution; preserve allocation/initialization and all existing forward functions except dispatch.

Its unchanged full packed helper uses Bx2x4x256 mass cells. New candidate uses Bx2x2x256 varying mass cells and reconstructs matched constants natively. Both are controls in the new common-source factorial.
